index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a hierarchical taxonomy of machine learning algorithms, structured as a top-down flowchart. At the apex is a rounded rectangular box labeled 'MACHINE LEARNING' in bold, uppercase, black text on a white background with a thin black border. From this root node, two thick blue arrows branch downward to two primary categories: 'SUPERVISED LEARNING' on the left and 'UNSUPERVISED LEARNING' on the right. Both are also rendered in bold, uppercase, black text within white rounded rectangles with thin black borders.

Under 'SUPERVISED LEARNING', two thick blue arrows extend downward to two secondary categories: 'CLASSIFICATION' and 'REGRESSION'. These are displayed in the same style as the primary categories. Under 'UNSUPERVISED LEARNING', a single thick blue arrow points to 'CLUSTERING', which follows the same visual format.

Beneath each of these three secondary categories, a vertical stack of light gray rounded rectangles lists specific algorithms. Each algorithm name is written in black, non-bold, title-case or sentence-case text. The 'CLASSIFICATION' column includes: Naive Bayes, Nearest Neighbor, Discriminant Analysis, Support Vector Machines, Decision Trees, Ensemble Methods, and Neural Networks. The 'REGRESSION' column contains: Linear Regression, GLM, and Gaussian Process. The 'CLUSTERING' column lists: K-Means, K-Medoids, Fuzzy C-Means, Hierarchical, Gaussian Mixture, DBSCAN, and Affinity Propagation Clustering.

All connections between nodes are represented by thick, solid blue arrows pointing from parent to child nodes, indicating a hierarchical relationship. The layout is symmetrical and organized into three vertical columns corresponding to the main branches: Classification (left), Regression (middle), and Clustering (right). The overall structure is clean, with consistent spacing and alignment, emphasizing the classification hierarchy of machine learning methods. The caption below the figure reads: 'A taxonomy of machine learning algorithms \citep{matlab}', indicating the source of the taxonomy.
